title: Polite requests are frames, not words
summary: Keep three ready frames with qǐng, kěyǐ…ma, and máfan, and politeness takes care of itself.
attribution: Original content authored for this project.

blocks.body: Everyday politeness in Chinese comes from framing a request rather than from long sentences. Three frames cover most of it: 请 qǐng plus the action, as in 请稍等 qǐng shāo děng (please wait a moment); 可以…吗 kěyǐ…ma for permission, as in 我可以坐这里吗? wǒ kěyǐ zuò zhèlǐ ma?; and 麻烦 máfan plus the person and the task, as in 麻烦您帮我一下 máfan nín bāng wǒ yíxià. Use 您 nín with a stranger who is helping you, and switch to 你 nǐ once you are among peers. End a soft suggestion with 吧 ba, and you will sound considerate without needing a longer vocabulary.
